### Building a New PC – Step‑by‑Step Guide Below is a practical, beginner‑friendly walkthrough. Feel free to skip sections you already know, but keep the order to avoid mistakes. | # | What to Do | Why It Matters | Tips | |---|------------|----------------|------| | 1 | **Plan & Budget** | Know what you’ll use it for (gaming, video editing, office work). | • List required specs: CPU, GPU, RAM, storage, PSU, case, cooling.
• Use PCPartPicker to check compatibility and price. | | 2 | **Gather Tools & Workspace** | A clean, static‑free environment prevents damage. | • 10‑mm Phillips screwdriver.
• Anti‑static wrist strap (optional but recommended).
• Flat, non‑metallic surface. | | 3 | **Open the Case** | Access the interior. | • Remove side panels (usually thumbscrews or a latch). | | 4 | **Install the Power Supply (PSU)** | Supplies power to all components. | • Align the PSU fan with the case vent.
• Secure with screws (usually 4).
• Route cables neatly; keep the cable management holes open. | | 5 | **Mount the Motherboard** | The backbone of the system. | • Place standoffs in the case to match the motherboard’s screw holes.
• Align the I/O shield with the rear panel.
• Screw the motherboard onto the standoffs. | | 6 | **Install the CPU** | Central processing unit. | • Lift the CPU socket lever.
• Align the CPU (triangle marker) with the socket.
• Gently place it, lower the lever. | | 7 | **Apply Thermal Paste & Install CPU Cooler** | Keeps the CPU from overheating. | • If the cooler has pre‑applied paste, skip this step.
• If not, apply a pea‑size amount on the CPU.
• Attach the cooler per its instructions (screws or clips). | | 8 | **Insert RAM Modules** | Memory for running programs. | • Open the RAM slots by pushing the side clips outward.
• Align the notch on the RAM with the slot key.
• Push firmly until the clips snap back. | | 9 | **Mount the Storage Drives** | SSDs/HDDs for data. | • 2.5″ SSDs: use a mounting bracket or a drive cage.
• 3.5″ HDDs: secure with screws.
• Connect SATA data & power cables. | | 10 | **Install the Graphics Card (GPU)** | Handles rendering for games, video, etc. | • Remove the appropriate rear expansion slot covers.
• Insert the GPU into the top PCI‑e x16 slot.
• Secure with screws. | | 11 | **Connect All Cables** | Power, data, front panel, fans. | • PSU to motherboard (24‑pin + 8‑pin CPU).
• PSU to GPU (6‑ or 8‑pin).
• SATA power/data to drives.
• Front panel connectors (USB, audio, power button). | | 12 | **Cable Management** | Improves airflow & aesthetics. | • Use zip ties or Velcro straps.
• Route cables through the cable‑management holes. | | 13 | **Close the Case** | Final assembly. | • Reattach side panels.
• Tighten all screws. | | 14 | **First Boot & BIOS Setup** | Verify hardware and set up. | • Connect monitor, keyboard, mouse.
• Power on.
• Enter BIOS (usually `Del` or `F2`).
• Check that all components are recognized. | | 15 | **Install Operating System (OS)** | Turn your PC into a usable computer. | • Create a bootable USB with Windows 10/11, Ubuntu, etc.
• Boot from USB, follow installation prompts. | | 16 | **Install Drivers & Updates** | Ensure optimal performance. | • Install motherboard chipset drivers.
• Install GPU drivers.
• Run Windows Update or equivalent. | | 17 | **Test & Benchmark** | Confirm stability. | • Run stress tests (Prime95, FurMark).
• Monitor temperatures (HWMonitor).
• Run benchmarks (Cinebench, 3DMark). | | 18 | **Enjoy & Maintain** | Keep your PC running smoothly. | • Clean dust every 3–6 months.
• Keep drivers updated.
• Monitor temperatures during heavy use. | --- #### Quick Checklist - [ ] **Case** – ATX, mid‑tower, or mini‑ITX? - [ ] **Motherboard** – ATX, micro‑ATX, or mini‑ITX; compatible with CPU socket. - [ ] **CPU** – Intel i5/i7/i9 or AMD Ryzen 5/7/9. - [ ] **GPU** – NVIDIA RTX 3060/3070/3080 or AMD Radeon RX 6600/6700/6800. - [ ] **RAM** – 16 GB DDR4/DDR5 (minimum 3200 MHz). - [ ] **Storage** – NVMe SSD (500 GB+) + optional SATA HDD. - [ ] **PSU** – 650 W–850 W, 80+ Gold or better. - [ ] **Cooling** – Stock cooler or aftermarket air/ liquid cooler. - [ ] **Case Fans** – 120 mm or 140 mm, 120 mm fans for intake/outlet. --- #### Common Pitfalls & How to Avoid Them | Issue | Fix | |-------|-----| | **Short‑circuit** | Ensure standoffs are correctly placed; never touch exposed metal contacts. | | **Overheating** | Verify thermal paste application; ensure GPU fans spin; keep case vents clear. | | **Component not recognized** | Double‑check BIOS settings; ensure all power connectors are seated. | | **No boot** | Verify boot order in BIOS; ensure OS USB is bootable. | | **Fan noise** | Tighten screws; use anti‑vibration mounts; check for dust. | --- #### Resources - **PCPartPicker** – Compatibility checker & price comparison. - **YouTube Channels** – Linus Tech Tips, JayzTwoCents, Paul's Hardware. - **Forums** – Tom’s Hardware, Reddit r/buildapc. - **Manuals** – Motherboard, PSU, GPU, case – usually PDF on manufacturer’s website. --- ### Final Thought Building a PC is a rewarding project that gives you full control over your machine’s performance and future upgrades. Take your time, double‑check every connection, and enjoy the process! If you hit a snag, feel free to ask for help. Happy building!
